STEP 1 - Scene: A small pile of raw/roasted whole almonds (brown, skin-on, some split halves) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a slight angle. It is a snack portion rather than a full meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 20 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2 (treating it as round-equivalent for a square plate, roughly 400 cm^2 for the full square; I use ~340 cm^2 as the usable vessel area).

STEP 3 - Items: Almonds only (about 35-40 whole almonds and halves).

STEP 4 - Area: The almond pile covers roughly 12% of the plate area, about 40 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height about 1.2 cm on average (almonds are ~2.5 cm long, mostly one layer with some stacking). 40 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 48 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are dense nuts with gaps; bulk density for whole nuts is about 0.5-0.6 g/ml. 48 ml x 0.55 ≈ 26 g. Check: 38 almonds at ~1.2 g each ≈ 45 g, so the counted estimate is higher; I take roughly 30 g as a compromise between the volume and count estimates.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw/dry-roasted almonds ≈ 580-610 kcal per 100 g. Using 600 kcal/100 g: 30 g x 6 = 180 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 30 g of almonds (roughly one small handful, ~35 nuts) at about 180 kcal is plausible for a visible snack portion.
